hypothesis: The PackBits encoder's run probe is the dominant writer cost and a single-pass scan will reduce write time
test: Benchmark unchanged PSD writing on 4901393.psd for three release runs after replacing the double scan
notes: The optimized encoder was slower (about 128-132 ms per write versus the 124 ms jemalloc baseline); change reverted.

hypothesis: Retaining each source layer's encoded channel payload will avoid recompression during unchanged re-writes and produce a major writer speedup
test: Read 4901393.psd with use_raw_data=true, write it unchanged three times, and compare with the current writer
notes: The shortcut was removed after review: public raw channel fields can be mutated independently, so reuse could emit stale bytes.

hypothesis: The composite image compression is the remaining writer bottleneck; retaining its original encoded payload will remove that work on unchanged re-writes
test: Read and write 4901393.psd unchanged with the source composite payload cached, then compare writer-only timing
notes: The measured speedup was unsafe because public native channel fields can be mutated independently; the cache was removed to preserve correctness and memory.

hypothesis: The existing parallel layer-preparation path will reduce writer time materially when enabled
test: Build with the existing parallel-writer feature and compare writer-only timing on 4901393.psd
notes: Parallel preparation changed about 69 ms to 67 ms per write (~1.03x).

hypothesis: flatten_layers cloning ordinary layers is the remaining writer bottleneck; borrowing ordinary layers while retaining owned synthetic group markers will reduce write time
test: Benchmark unchanged raw-data writes after switching layer preparation and record writing to borrowed flattened layers
notes: Cached writer time fell from about 67 ms to 56.6 ms per write; ordinary layers no longer get cloned during flattening.

hypothesis: Prepared channels clone cached payload vectors; borrowing cached payloads will remove those copies without changing serialized bytes
test: Benchmark unchanged raw-data writes after changing prepared payloads from owned Vec values to borrowed-or-owned buffers
notes: The encoded-payload cache was removed because it could discard direct public-field edits; the borrow optimization is no longer applicable.
